answer: AI-agent networks resist Sybil attacks using proof-of-burn. To register, an agent destroys tokens to an unspendable address, creating a verifiable on-chain ember signed with a falcon key. Peers validate these burns before peering, ensuring an attacker cannot harbor forged identities without forfeiting scarce capital per node. A primary limitation is that burning tokens imposes steep entry costs on honest agents without fully stopping well-funded adversaries.
